name: rods-vo-1
text: Every Indian street has this... and it's not an accident. [short pause] Steel rods, sticking out of the roof. They're the tops of the columns... left there on purpose. Because most Indian homes are built the way money comes in. One floor now... the next one when the family grows. [short pause] Here's the logic. A new floor's columns have to lock into the old ones. Leave the rods out... and that joint is ready. Cut them off... and later, someone has to drill into the columns and glue new bars in. [short pause] But there's a catch. Bare steel rusts. And rust can swell up to six times bigger than the steel it eats. Rain runs down the rods... into the column... and the concrete can crack from the inside. So... is it a plan, or a slow problem? Rods on your roof: future floor... or future crack?
